title: Sigstore Offline Kit — Tools & Components Reference
subtitle: What every tool is, why the kit uses it, and where it appears

categories.name: Workstation tools
categories.intro: Command-line tools you run on the laptop (Linux or WSL2). All except the OS basics are downloaded once by 01-build-offline-bundle.sh into bundle/bin, so nothing is installed from the internet on the offline machine.

tools.name: Docker (Engine / Desktop)
tools.what: Container runtime that runs Linux containers on your machine.
tools.why: Everything runs in containers: the kind Kubernetes node, the offline image mirror, and the TUF repository builder. Docker Desktop provides this on Windows via WSL2.

tools.name: WSL2 (Windows only)
tools.what: Windows Subsystem for Linux — a real Linux kernel inside Windows.
tools.why: All kit scripts are bash. WSL2 gives Windows users the same shell, tools and paths as Linux users, and Docker Desktop integrates with it.

tools.name: kind
tools.what: Kubernetes IN Docker — runs a full Kubernetes cluster as Docker containers.
tools.why: Gives a real, disposable Kubernetes v1.37 cluster on a laptop, using the same Helm charts as production. Its containerd honours /etc/containerd/certs.d, which is how the cluster pulls images from the offline mirror.
tools.offline: Binary in bundle/bin; node image kindest/node:v1.37.0 in host-images.tar.

tools.name: kubectl
tools.why: Creates namespaces and Secrets (keys, TLS), applies manifests, waits for rollouts, reads logs and runs admission dry-runs.

tools.name: Helm
tools.what: Package manager for Kubernetes; installs versioned charts with a values file.
tools.why: Installs Traefik, Trillian, Rekor, Fulcio, the CT log and Kyverno from the official charts, pinned to tested versions, using the kit's values files.
tools.offline: Binary in bundle/bin; charts as .tgz in bundle/charts.

tools.name: crane
tools.what: Daemonless tool for working with container images and registries.
tools.why: Builds the offline mirror (crane copy keeps multi-arch digests intact), resolves image digests before signing, pushes the demo image without needing Docker to trust the CA, and lists tags.
tools.offline: Binary in bundle/bin (+ crane.exe for Windows).

tools.name: cosign
tools.why: Performs keyless signing (OIDC login → Fulcio certificate → Rekor entry), verifies signatures, attaches attestations, and generates the private trusted_root.json and signing_config.json.
tools.offline: Binary in bundle/bin (+ cosign.exe for Windows).

tools.name: gitsign
tools.what: Sigstore's keyless signer for git commits and tags; git calls it in place of GPG (gpg.format x509, gpg.x509.program gitsign).
tools.why: Proves who wrote each commit with the same Keycloak login, private Fulcio CA and Rekor log as image signing, so there are no GPG or SSH signing keys to manage.
tools.offline: Binary in bundle/bin (+ gitsign.exe for Windows), checked against the release checksums.txt.

tools.name: jq
tools.why: Reads OIDC tokens, Rekor API responses, trusted roots and Kyverno output inside the scripts.

tools.name: OpenSSL
tools.why: Generates every key and certificate locally: TLS root and wildcard cert, Fulcio root + intermediate CA, Rekor and CT log signing keys. Also verifies chains and compares key fingerprints.

tools.name: curl
tools.why: Health checks against Keycloak, Fulcio, Rekor, registry and TUF over TLS, and fetching OIDC tokens for non-interactive signing.

tools.name: bash, perl, coreutils
tools.what: Shell and standard Unix utilities (tar, sha256sum, base64, sed, awk).
tools.why: bash runs the scripts; perl renders the .tpl templates; sha256sum verifies the bundle; tar/base64 package the TUF repo and backups.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.why: Edits the Windows hosts file and imports the TLS root into the Windows certificate store, so browsers, Docker Desktop and cosign.exe trust *.sigstore.local.

categories.name: Cluster platform
categories.intro: Infrastructure the Sigstore services need: networking, DNS, storage, ingress and the image supply. None of it is Sigstore-specific, but each piece solves a concrete offline problem.

tools.name: containerd (in the kind node)
tools.what: The container runtime Kubernetes uses to pull and run images.
tools.why: Configured through hosts.toml files to fetch docker.io, ghcr.io, quay.io, gcr.io, registry.k8s.io and reg.kyverno.io images from the local mirror, and to trust the private registry's TLS certificate.
tools.cmd: docker exec sigstore-control-plane crictl pull ghcr.io/sigstore/fulcio:v1.9.0

tools.name: Offline image mirror (registry:2)
tools.what: A registry container on 127.0.0.1:5000 serving bundle/mirror.
tools.why: Replaces the internet for image pulls. Every platform image is stored as <registry>/<repo> with its original digest, so the Helm charts' digest-pinned references work unchanged.
tools.offline: Image in host-images.tar; data in bundle/mirror (≈4.2 GB).

tools.name: Traefik
tools.what: Kubernetes ingress controller and reverse proxy.
tools.why: Single TLS front door for keycloak, fulcio, rekor, registry and tuf .sigstore.local. Pinned to ClusterIP 10.96.100.100 so pods and the node resolve the same names to it. Chosen because ingress-nginx was retired in March 2026.

tools.name: CoreDNS
tools.why: An extra sigstore.local zone answers every *.sigstore.local name with Traefik's IP, so Fulcio can reach Keycloak and Kyverno can reach the registry/TUF through the same TLS endpoints as the laptop.

tools.name: local-path-provisioner
tools.what: Dynamic storage provisioner backed by node disk.
tools.why: Creates the PersistentVolumes for MySQL (transparency logs), the registry, Keycloak and Rekor attestation storage.

categories.name: Sigstore services
categories.intro: The core of the stack — private replacements for fulcio.sigstore.dev, rekor.sigstore.dev and the public CT log, all signing with keys you generated.

tools.name: Fulcio
tools.why: Turns a verified OIDC identity into a 10-minute X.509 signing certificate, issued by your intermediate CA. Trusts Keycloak through the CACert field and submits every certificate to the CT log.

tools.name: CT log (ct_server / ctfe)
tools.why: Records every certificate Fulcio issues and returns a Signed Certificate Timestamp (SCT) embedded in the cert, so mis-issued certificates are detectable. cosign verifies the SCT.

tools.name: Rekor
tools.what: Sigstore's transparency log for signatures and attestations.
tools.why: Stores a tamper-evident record of every signature and returns an inclusion proof and signed timestamp, proving the signature was made while the short-lived certificate was valid. Uses your file-based signer key.

tools.name: Trillian (log server + log signer)
tools.why: The storage engine under both Rekor and the CT log. The log server accepts entries and serves proofs; the log signer sequences them into the tree.

tools.name: MySQL (trillian db_server)
tools.why: Persists Trillian's Merkle trees — the complete transparency history. The most important data to back up.

tools.name: Redis
tools.why: Rekor's search index (artifact hash → entry UUID). Rebuildable from the log, so not backed up.

categories.name: Identity, trust & storage
categories.short: Who signs, what to trust, where artifacts live
categories.intro: The pieces that decide who may sign, how every client learns which keys to trust, and where signed images and their signatures are stored.

tools.name: Keycloak
tools.why: Private replacement for Google/GitHub/Microsoft login. Issues the OIDC tokens Fulcio exchanges for certificates: browser, device-code and password flows for people (alice@sigstore.local), client_credentials for CI (ci@sigstore.local).
tools.offline: Image mirrored; realm imported from a Secret.

tools.name: Private OCI registry (registry:2)
tools.why: Stores your images and, next to them, the Sigstore signature and attestation bundles. Served at https://registry.sigstore.local behind Traefik TLS.

tools.name: TUF repository (scaffolding server)
tools.what: The Update Framework — signed metadata for distributing trust files.
tools.why: Distributes trusted_root.json and signing_config securely and supports rotation. Clients pin one root.json; Kyverno 1.19 requires a TUF source to verify keyless signatures offline.
tools.offline: Builder image in host-images.tar; server image mirrored.

tools.name: Private PKI (generated)
tools.what: Two separate certificate hierarchies plus log keys.
tools.why: TLS root + wildcard cert protect transport; Fulcio root (offline) + intermediate (EKU codeSigning) anchor code signing; Rekor and CT keys sign log evidence. Separate hierarchies so one compromise doesn't imply the other.

categories.name: Policy enforcement
categories.intro: Admission controllers that check images before Kubernetes runs them.

tools.name: Kyverno
tools.why: Its ImageValidatingPolicy verifies every Pod image from registry.sigstore.local carries a keyless signature from your Fulcio/Rekor with an allowed identity, using trust from the private TUF mirror. Tested: signed admitted, unsigned denied.

tools.name: OPA Gatekeeper (optional)
tools.what: Policy engine using the Rego language.
tools.why: Cannot verify cosign signatures itself; the kit uses it to require images from the private registry pinned by digest, alongside Kyverno.
tools.offline: Install from your own mirror if used.

tools.name: Sigstore policy-controller (reference)
tools.why: Alternative to Kyverno using TrustRoot + ClusterImagePolicy. Provided as an untested reference.

categories.name: Helper container images
categories.intro: Small images the charts and scripts run once or in init containers. They appear in bundle/images.txt and you may see them in kubectl get pods.

tools.name: scaffolding createdb
tools.why: Creates the trillian database schema in MySQL on first install.

tools.name: scaffolding createtree
tools.why: Creates a Trillian tree for Rekor and for the CT log and stores its ID in a ConfigMap (rekor-config / ctlog-config). Skips if an ID already exists — which is what makes restore work.
tools.cmd: kubectl -n rekor-system get cm rekor-config -o yaml

tools.name: scaffolding createctconfig
tools.why: Builds the CT log configuration: fetches Fulcio's root, loads your CT key from Secret ctlog-signer, writes Secret ctlog-secret.

tools.name: curlimages/curl
tools.why: Init containers that wait for Trillian / Fulcio to answer before Rekor and the CT config job start.

tools.name: busybox
tools.what: Minimal Linux userland in one image.
tools.why: Trillian init containers, the TUF unpack init container, DNS check pods, the Keycloak restore pod, and the demo app's base image.

tools.name: Kyverno helper images
tools.why: Pre-start cleanup, CLI used by chart hooks, and readiness checks for the Kyverno install.

categories.name: Build & test tools
categories.intro: Not needed to run the stack. Used to prove the kit works (test/compose/run.sh) and to lint it. Useful if you change the kit.

tools.name: Docker Compose
tools.what: Runs multi-container apps from one YAML file.
tools.why: Runs the same Sigstore images and arguments as the charts, without Kubernetes, for the end-to-end offline integration test.

tools.name: nginx (test gateway)
tools.why: Stands in for Traefik in the Docker test: TLS termination and the *.sigstore.local names.

tools.name: Toolbox image (buildpack-deps)
tools.what: Debian image with bash, curl, openssl.
tools.why: A stand-in laptop on an --internal network with no internet, proving every client step works air-gapped.

tools.name: createtree (Trillian CLI)
tools.why: Creates Trillian trees in the Docker test (in Kubernetes the createtree Job does it).

tools.name: Kyverno CLI
tools.why: Proved the ImageValidatingPolicy admits signed and denies unsigned images, against the live registry and TUF.

tools.name: gator
tools.why: Validated the Gatekeeper digest/registry constraint.

tools.name: shellcheck
tools.why: Linted every script for bugs.

tools.name: kubeconform
tools.why: Validated the registry, Keycloak and TUF manifests against the Kubernetes API schema.
